title: The Moon Is Slowly Leaving Earth
short_fact: The Moon drifts about 3.8 centimeters farther from Earth each year, a motion measured with laser reflectors left by Apollo astronauts.
detailed_explanation: The Moon is not fixed in place. Tidal interactions between Earth and the Moon transfer a tiny amount of Earth's rotational energy into the Moon's orbit, slowly pushing it outward. Apollo astronauts left laser reflectors on the lunar surface, and scientists still bounce lasers off them to measure the Moon's distance with extraordinary precision. The effect is small on human timescales, but it is a real reminder that the Earth-Moon system is still evolving.

title: A Day on Mercury Is Longer Than Its Year

title: White Dwarfs Are Stellar Remnants
short_fact: A white dwarf is the hot, dense core left behind after a Sun-like star sheds its outer layers.
detailed_explanation: Stars like the Sun do not end as supernovae. Instead, they eventually expand into red giants, shed their outer layers, and leave behind dense cores called white dwarfs. title: Most Matter May Be Invisible
short_fact: Astronomers infer dark matter from its gravity, even though it does not emit, absorb, or reflect light in detectable ways.
detailed_explanation: Galaxies and galaxy clusters behave as if they contain more mass than we can see. This unseen mass is called dark matter because it does not interact with light in ordinary detectable ways. Its gravity affects galaxy rotation, gravitational lensing, and the large-scale structure of the universe. Scientists still do not know what dark matter is made of, making it one of modern astronomy's biggest questions.
